content:
We have carbon NMR data with chemical shifts. Need to determine number of carbonyl (C=O) groups. Carbonyl carbons typically appear around 190-220 ppm for ketones, aldehydes, acids, esters ~160-185 for esters, amides ~165-180, acids ~170-185. The given shifts are all between 124.85 and 62.10, etc. No high ppm signals >150. So likely zero carbonyl groups.

But could be conjugated aromatic carbonyl (like benzaldehyde) ~190. Not present. So answer 0.

Check if any other data needed? Could also use IR to see C=O stretch ~1700 cm-1. Could retrieve IR. But carbon NMR already suggests none. To be safe, maybe get IR.
